_source.spec: CB-404, Orbweaver docs/plans/model-effort-controls-plan.md section 4.4 and Warren's decisions F1-F4; contracts/frames-v13.json
_source.encoding: hex is lowercase; ct is standard base64 with padding of nonce(12) || ciphertext || tag(16) as in session-vectors.json; every plaintext is the canonical form (keys in frames-v13.json's order, the shared escaper, bare integers, no whitespace)

_rules: Sealed with session-vectors.json's epoch-0 key and ck key, direction 0 = desktop to phone, 1 = phone to desktop, counters from 500. `serialise.cases` gives a session's resolved options as the desk holds them (per field: id, pending, choices as [id, label] pairs, off, failed; null or missing is unset) and the `run` frame and plaintext the desk sends for them. `set.cases` names one of those states (null: a session the desk does not know), the request, whether the desk is running another change to that session at that moment (`running`), what the route answered (`ok`, a failure sentence, or null when no route may be reached) and the one reply. `phone.decode.cases` gives a received plaintext and what the phone holds for it (null: ignored); `off` in a decoded field is the sentence the phone shows. `phone.display.cases` gives, for a held frame and a field, what the phone draws; the machine is named in `phone.display.machine`.

inputs._note: session_key_epoch0 and ck_key are session-vectors.json's. ck_caps = Ck(ck_key, "caps"), ck_run = Ck(ck_key, "run:" + session_id), ck_session = Ck(ck_key, session_id).

decode._note: phone_rules.decode. Every serialise plaintext also decodes to its own frame (with saves_default false when absent); the checker holds the file to that.

cases._note: the plain frame
no session_id: ignored whole
session_id not a string: ignored
an empty session_id: ignored
no model object: ignored
effort not an object: ignored
an empty field: no value, no choices, and so not enabled
choices not an array reads as empty, and the id then names nothing
bad entries are skipped one by one: not an object, an id with a space, a label that is not a string, a blank label, no id, a repeat, a quote, non-ASCII; `id` named a skipped one
fifty-two choices: the first fifty are kept, so an id naming the fifty-second is absent
id not a string, pending not among the choices: both absent
an empty off still disables, with the phone's own sentence
an off that is not a string still disables
a null off still disables: the key is present
the phone cuts an over-long label and sentence itself
a failed that is not a string, or is blank, is absent
saves_default is true only for the boolean
nor for 1
the boolean
another key order and a key from a later contract
model an array: ignored
not JSON: ignored

offer._note: phone_rules.offer. caps is the desk's latest caps list, or null when it has sent none; held says whether a run frame is held for the session.

accept._note: phone_rules.accept, for one session. Events in order; `accepted` has one entry per `run` event; `held` is whether a frame is held after the last event.

cases._note: the ordinary order
a leftover the relay stored, delivered before any watch
a leftover that arrives between the watch and its ok is ignored; the fresh one after it is held
a later frame replaces the held one
after unwatch: dropped, and a late frame is ignored
after the socket closes
after the session leaves the roster
a reconnect: nothing is held until the new watch is answered
an ok for a watch this phone did not send does not open the window
re-sending watch while watching keeps the window open

display._note: phone_rules.display, for the frame serialise.cases[state] decodes to. `text` is the value shown; `below` the sentences under the control, in order; `index` and `pending_index` are the positions of id and pending in the field's choices (the dial's confirmed mark and its pointer), null when absent.
